samples.summary: The nesting-cap predicate is implemented twice, once per package, instead of once in the shared `@wafflebase/docs` module that already owns the constant. `hasDocsTableAtNestingCap` / `documentHasTableAtNestingCap` (packages/backend/src/yorkie/docs-tree.ts:231-256) and `hasTableAtNestingCap` (packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:454-465) are byte-for-byte the same walk over the same `Block[]` shape, down to the identical refusal message string in `writeDocsRoot` (docs-tree.ts:376) and `writeFullDocument` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:3337). `MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH` was correctly put in `packages/docs/src/model/table-nesting.ts` and exported from BOTH entry points (`src/index.ts` and `src/node.ts`) precisely so frontend and backend could share it — the predicate that reads it could have travelled the same way (backend `docs-tree.ts` already imports `docsTreeToDocument`, `serializeBlockStyleAttrs` from `@wafflebase/docs`). The repo's stated expectation is reuse; two copies of the same invariant are two places to change when the cap semantics move (e.g. `>=` vs `>`, or header/footer coverage), and the copies will then give two answers to the question "may this document be written?" on the two sides of the same CRDT.
samples.evidence: backend docs-tree.ts:231 `export function hasDocsTableAtNestingCap(blocks, depth = 0)` vs frontend yorkie-doc-store.ts:454 `function hasTableAtNestingCap(blocks, depth = 0)` — identical bodies; backend's own docstring says "The same read cap seen from the write side that the frontend store applies (`hasTableAtNestingCap` in `yorkie-doc-store.ts`)".

samples.summary: The design doc section this change adds asserts "**Producers** never create one past it: … paste drops the tables in a fragment that would (`capTableNesting`, counted against the paste target's own depth)" (docs/design/docs/tables/docs-nested-tables.md:293-296), but only ONE of the two paste branches is capped. `handlePaste` dispatches to `insertBlocks` (capped at text-editor.ts:4568) or to `pasteTableCells` (text-editor.ts:4698), and the cell-range branch clones the clipboard `TableCell[][]` straight into the target cells (`td.rows[targetRow].cells[targetCol] = cloned`, line 4749) with no depth check at all. A clipboard cell payload may legally carry nested tables (the sanitizer's own `MAX_TABLE_DEPTH` = 8 permits them, clipboard.ts:72), so pasting such cells into a cell already ~25 tables deep produces exactly the state the cap exists to prevent — and since `buildBlockNode` then writes any table at/past the cap with `children: []`, the pasted rows are silently dropped into the CRDT rather than refused. The stated invariant therefore does not hold for the cell-rectangle paste, which is the paste path most likely to carry tables.
samples.evidence: text-editor.ts:4740-4751 copies cells with `cloneTableCells` and no `capTableNesting` / `tableNestingDepth` call; the only capped call site is line 4568 inside `insertBlocks`.
searchedFor: grep capTableNesting|tableNestingDepth across repo (only editor.ts:4232, document.ts:925, text-editor.ts:4568)

samples.summary: The REST validator is now one level STRICTER than the writer it validates for, so a document the editor and `writeDocsRoot` both accept cannot be PUT back. `assertValidBlock` rejects any block — including an ordinary paragraph — at `depth >= MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH`, and its `depth` counts table-cell descents exactly as the readers do. A chain of 32 tables (depths 0…31) is fully materialized by `treeNodeToBlock`, is NOT flagged by `documentHasTableAtNestingCap` (which only flags a *table* at depth >= cap), and is created happily by the editor (`insertTableInCell` refuses only at depth >= 32, i.e. after 32 tables) — yet its innermost cell's paragraph sits at depth 32 and now 400s. That breaks the `GET` → edit → `PUT` identity this same file treats as a first-class contract, for the deepest document the rest of the system calls legal. Either the validator should reject at `depth > MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH`, or the whole stack should agree on 31 tables.
samples.evidence: controller line 454 `if (depth >= MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH)` vs docs-tree.ts:231-240 which flags only `block.type === 'table'` at `depth >= MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH`.

samples.summary: Scope breadth: the PR bundles at least four independent themes under one change. (1) The #1049 fix proper — nested-table-aware lookups in `normalizeRange`, `getSelectedText`, `getSelectedTableCells`, and the unified `resolveCellGesture` for drag/shift+click. (2) A whole table-nesting-cap subsystem across two packages, the backend REST validator and `DocumentCopyService`. (3) `blockParentMap` cycle guards in six unrelated walks (`findBlockInCells`, `resolvePositionPixel`, `walkToTopLevelBlockId`, `resolveNestedTableLayout`, `findOuterCellAddress`, `moveToNext/PrevCell`). (4) A render-path work budget (`MAX_MERGE_EXPANSION_CELLS`), presence `tableCellRange` clamping, and a spread→reduce fold in `range-slices.ts`. Only themes (1) and (2) are recorded in the design doc; (3) and (4) are hardening with no stated driver in the diff. Each is defensible on its own, but they land together in ~20 files, which makes the change hard to review, bisect or revert as a unit.
samples.evidence: selection.ts adds MAX_MERGE_EXPANSION_CELLS + clampCellIndex + walkToTopLevelBlockId alongside the #1049 nested-table lookup; range-slices.ts:56 folds `Math.max(...rows)`; peer-cursor.ts:122 adds a cycle guard — none of which the #1049 selection defect requires.

samples.summary: Only one of the cross-cutting invariants this change introduces is written down. The nesting ceiling gets a proper §7 in the canonical nested-tables doc (good — folded into the existing doc rather than a parallel one). The other two architectural rules the change establishes are recorded only in code comments: (a) "block ids arrive verbatim from peer-written CRDT attributes, so a parent chain that loops back on itself is representable" — now a standing invariant enforced in six `blockParentMap` walks across `document.ts`, `selection.ts`, `peer-cursor.ts`, `table-layout.ts` and `text-editor.ts`; and (b) the render path is now budget-bounded (`MAX_MERGE_EXPANSION_CELLS`) and presence `tableCellRange` indices are clamped to the table — neither mentioned in `docs-presence.md` or `docs-tables.md`. The next contributor adding a `blockParentMap` walk or a presence-driven loop has no doc telling them these bounds are mandatory.
samples.evidence: docs/design/docs/tables/docs-nested-tables.md §7 covers only MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH; grep for `cycle|blockParentMap` across docs/design returns no docs match for the parent-map cycle invariant, and docs-presence.md mentions clamping only for label x-position (lines 232, 530).

samples.summary: `expandCellRangeForMerges` now answers two different questions depending on an optional argument: exact for every command/write caller, deliberately approximate for the one render-path caller. The shape is documented at length, but a shared helper whose correctness contract flips on a defaulted parameter is easy to mis-call — a future caller that feeds the result to `mergeCells` and happens to pass a budget (copying the `normalizeCellRange` call site) gets a rectangle that slices an existing merge, with no type-level signal. Splitting the two uses into two named entry points (as was done for `findMergeTopLeft` / `findMergeTopLeftBudgeted` immediately above) would make the exact-vs-painted distinction unmistakable at every call site.
samples.evidence: selection.ts:118 `export function expandCellRangeForMerges(cr, table, budgetCells = Infinity)`; the budgeted variant of `findMergeTopLeft` was given its own private name instead.

verdict.reason: Verified in the tree. `hasDocsTableAtNestingCap` (packages/backend/src/yorkie/docs-tree.ts:231-245) and `hasTableAtNestingCap` (packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:454-465) are the same walk over the same block shape with the same `depth >= MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH` cap and the same recursion into `cell.blocks`; the header/footer coverage (docs-tree.ts:250-256 vs yorkie-doc-store.ts:3332-3334) and the refusal message (docs-tree.ts:377-381 vs yorkie-doc-store.ts:3336-3340) are duplicated verbatim. The backend docstring itself names the frontend twin (docs-tree.ts:224-225). A shared home exists and is already on both import paths: MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH in packages/docs/src/model/table-nesting.ts:26, exported from src/index.ts:97 and src/node.ts:145, with related nesting logic already in @wafflebase/docs (model/document.ts:158-170, model/crdt-tree.ts:225); backend docs-tree.ts:35-41 already imports from that package. Both copies are live write gates (document-copy.service.ts:446 calls writeDocsRoot; writeFullDocument gates the header/footer path), so neither is unreachable. Duplication/reuse is in this lens's lane and this is the rubric's named major case: one invariant, two copies, two possible answers to "may this document be written?" on the two sides of the same CRDT. The only nuance found — backend uses its own DocsBlock type from ./yorkie.types — argues for a structural signature on the extracted helper, not against the duplication being real.

verdict.reason: The absence claim holds. `capTableNesting` has exactly one production call site (text-editor.ts:4568-4571, inside `insertBlocks`); the sibling paste branch `pasteTableCells` (text-editor.ts:4698-4766) clones clipboard cells into the target table (4716-4717, 4748-4749) with no depth check, and nothing upstream caps it: `handlePaste` (1746-1760) hands `data.tableCells` straight to `applyPastePlan`, which dispatches to `pasteTableCells` (1575), and `planPaste` (1526-1541) returns tableCells plans unmodified. The payload can legally carry nested tables — `deserializeClipboard` sanitizes cell rows at depth 0 (clipboard.ts:470) with `MAX_TABLE_DEPTH = 8` (clipboard.ts:72,309), and `getSelectedTableCells` (4317-4347) copies nested-table cells verbatim while `cloneTableCells` (clipboard.ts:477-491) does no depth work. Downstream, `updateBlockDirect` -> `YorkieDocStore.updateBlock` -> `buildBlockNode` truncates any table at/past the cap to `children: []` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:397-400, 1756), i.e. the pasted rows are silently dropped rather than refused, and the local cache keeps the uncapped block (1760), so cache and CRDT diverge. That write-layer bound prevents the stack-overflow hazard but is precisely the degraded outcome the finding names; the design doc's stated producer invariant (docs/design/docs/tables/docs-nested-tables.md:293-296) does not hold for the cell-rectangle paste. I could not refute it on any ground.

finding.summary: The backend v1 PUT writer — a duplicate producer of the same Yorkie tree — keeps its own, differently-bounded depth constant, so the producer cap this delta argues for is not enforced there
finding.evidence: The delta's stated design (`docx-importer.ts:244-256`, yorkie-doc-store.ts:3248-3258) is "cap the producer so the consumers are safe", and it caps the DOCX importer and the frontend full-document writer. But `packages/backend/src/yorkie/docs-tree.ts:150-200` is a verbatim second copy of `buildBlockNode`/`buildRowNode`/`buildCellNode` writing the SAME tree from a REST `PUT /content` body, and it received no cap; its only bound is `assertValidBlock`'s independent `MAX_ELEMENT_DEPTH = 32` (controller line 806) tested as `depth > MAX_ELEMENT_DEPTH` (line 443), i.e. it ADMITS 33 nested table blocks, one deeper than `MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH`'s `depth >= 32` truncation. Two writers now give two answers to "how deep may a table be", and the API answer produces exactly the document this delta declares must never exist: a table at a depth every reader materializes as rows-less, which `writeFullDocument` then refuses to rewrite, so it cannot be repaired from the editor. Cost is outside tidiness (silently truncated, unrepairable user content via an authenticated endpoint) and the divergence is introduced by this change.

verdict.reason: All three load-bearing factual claims are contradicted by the code. (1) The finding says `packages/backend/src/yorkie/docs-tree.ts` buildBlockNode "received no cap"; it has exactly that cap at line 179 (`depth >= MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH ? [] : ...`), using the shared constant imported from `@wafflebase/docs` at line 38, with `depth` a required (non-defaulted) parameter at line 162 and threaded through buildCellNode (line 207) and buildRowNode (line 215). (2) The finding says the REST PUT path's only bound is `assertValidBlock`'s local `MAX_ELEMENT_DEPTH` tested with `>`; assertValidBlock at docs-content.controller.ts:439 actually tests `depth >= MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH` at line 454 using the shared constant imported at line 49, and the comment at lines 446-453 explicitly rejects the local-constant/`>` formulation by name. `MAX_ELEMENT_DEPTH` (line 817) is used only at lines 851 and 1191, both slides element/text walks that do not produce the docs Yorkie tree. (3) The finding says the API "ADMITS 33 nested table blocks"; `>=` at line 454 with `depth + 1` recursion at line 502 rejects at depth 32, admitting 0-31 — identical to the writer's bound. There is therefore no divergence between the two producers. Independently, the claimed unrepairable-document consequence is blocked anyway: writeDocsRoot throws on `documentHasTableAtNestingCap` at docs-tree.ts:376-382 (predicate at lines 231-256) before mutating the tree, covered by a test at docs-tree.spec.ts:741-749.

finding.summary: Interactive producers (insert-table-in-cell, paste) still write past the cap through granular CRDT ops, so the producer-side argument only covers the DOCX path
finding.evidence: The delta justifies the import cap as "an imported document must never *contain* a table at a depth the readers truncate" (docx-importer.ts:432-441). The same invariant is not enforced on the editor's own producers: `Document.insertTableInCell` (packages/docs/src/model/document.ts:885, driven by editor.ts:4237) carries no depth check, and the paste sanitizer bounds only the *relative* depth of the pasted payload with its own separate constant `MAX_TABLE_DEPTH = 8` (clipboard.ts:71) — pasting an 8-deep table into an already-deep cell yields an absolute depth past 32. Those paths write via granular tree ops, bypassing `writeFullDocument`'s new refusal, so a user can still commit a table at a depth every reader shows as rows-less (silent content loss on next load) and which now also makes any later full write throw. Also a second, differently-scaled nesting constant in the same package for the same concept.

verdict.reason: All three specifics of the finding are contradicted by the tree. (1) `Document.insertTableInCell` does carry the depth check: document.ts:919-930 throws when `tableNestingDepth(blockId) >= MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH` (the reviewer cited line 885; the function is at 913). (2) The interactive editor command guards before writing: editor.ts:4229-4234 returns early at the cap, deliberately checked before the block split. (3) Paste enforces the ABSOLUTE cap, not merely relative depth: `capTableNesting` (clipboard.ts:429-447) compares against `MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH` and is invoked from text-editor.ts:4568-4571 as `capTableNesting(incoming, this.doc.tableNestingDepth(pos.blockId))` — precisely the "8-deep fragment into an already-deep cell" scenario the finding says is unhandled. The "two differently-scaled constants" point is also not an accidental duplicate: clipboard.ts:415-428 documents MAX_TABLE_DEPTH=8 as the untrusted-payload parse-recursion bound versus MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH as the absolute tree invariant. Tests cover all of it at test/model/table-nesting.test.ts:136-201. One residual I did find and am reporting for honesty: `pasteTableCells` (text-editor.ts:4698-4740) does not call capTableNesting, but that is a narrow line-level correctness gap requiring a >=24-deep host table, in another lens, and is not the claim raised.
